html:
In 1042 the Indian Buddhist teacher Atisha arrived in western Tibet. His teaching led the "second spread" of Buddhism in Tibet.

Buddhism had first come to Tibet under the Tibetan Empire, but when the empire broke up in the 840s, monasteries lost their patrons and the faith declined. In the 10th and 11th centuries the kings of Guge, in far western Tibet, set out to revive it. They sent young men to India to study and invited Indian masters.

Atisha was a Bengali monk, born in 982, and one of the leading teachers at the great monastery of Vikramashila under the Pala Empire. After several invitations from Guge, he agreed to come, a journey told under Atisha travels to Tibet. He meant to stay a few years but never went back. He died near Lhasa in 1054.

His short text A Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment set out an orderly path for all kinds of students. His disciple Dromtön founded the Kadam school. In the 14th century Tsongkhapa built on Kadam teaching to found the Gelug school, so Atisha's ideas run through the school of the Dalai Lamas.
sum: In 1042 the Indian Buddhist teacher Atisha arrived in western Tibet. His teaching led the "second spread" of Buddhism in Tibet.
